previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute-on-chronic left hip pain. He presented with worsening pain, chills, and elevated inflammatory markers, raising concern for septic arthritis. Imaging showed no fracture, and joint aspiration revealed no infection on gram stain or culture, supporting a diagnosis of left hip synovitis. He was treated with IV methylprednisolone and a fluoroscopic-guided steroid injection into the left hip, with subsequent improvement in pain and mobility. An MRI showed stable chronic sacroiliitis and worsening degenerative disc disease. His asthma and sleep apnea were managed with home medications and CPAP. He was discharged home ambulatory with a pain regimen, follow-up plans with rheumatology, and instructions to monitor for signs of infection.
problems: Other synovitis and tenosynovitis, left thigh
Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing 
spondylitis (previously trialed on Sulfasalazine, Etanercept, 
Adalimumab, Infliximab, and Golimumab x 1 c/b respiratory 
infection; not currently on immunosuppression), HTN, OSA, and 
asthma with recent admission ___ for acute-on-chronic left 
hip pain who re-presented for worsening R hip and bilateral SI 
joint pain. 

# Ankylosing spondylitis, resulting in R hip pain: The patient 
reported progressing R hip pain and found to have limited AROM 
and PROM on exam ___ to pain bilaterally. He also endorsed 
bilateral SI joint pain. Clinical picture was consistent with 
inflammatory synovitis secondary to progressing AS. CRP was 
reassuring at 9.6 compared to 35.7 on last admission. He was 
initially unable to tolerate PO pain meds due to nausea and was 
treated with IV dilaudid ___ Q4H. He was quickly transitioned 
to his home pain med regimen of Ibuprofen, Acetaminophen, and 
Oxycodone with PO dilaudid ___ for breakthrough pain. 
Rheumatology was consulted and recommended ___ R hip 
steroid injection, which he received on ___. The patient's R 
hip pain improved, however flank pain R>L continued to worsen. 
Rheumatology did not think systemic steroids were an appropriate 
treatment for the patient's pain and patient was counseled 
extensively on this recommendation. The patient was instead 
started on cyclobenzaprine 10mg for muscle pain. The patient 
developed anterior chest pain with tenderness to palpation over 
his ribs, concerning for chostochondritis vs osteitis. Bone scan 
was performed which showed increased uptake in bilateral knees, 
shoulders and sternoclavicular joints all consistent with 
degenerative disease, but not with acute inflammation.  Systemic 
steroids were not prescribed, given the adverse effects and 
limited benefit.  Overall, it appears that he is unlikely to 
have significant improvement in his pain unless he begins 
immunosuppresive treatment for his AS.  Given prior infectious 
complications, he is not willing to consider this treatment at 
this point. Rehabilitation was recommended to try to improve his 
mobility.  

# Hematuria/proteinuria: pt with stable hematuria and trace 
proteinuria on admission and repeat UA. Appeared stable from 
early ___. Patient would benefit from outpatient work-up with 
urology.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Asthma: The patient was continued on his home ipratropium and 
albuterol 2 puffs each BID and home montelukast 10mg daily. His 
home Budesonide was held as it was non-formulary and replaced 
with flovent HFA 110 mcg 1 puff BID while in-house.

# Anxiety: Continued home Sertraline 100mg QHS.

# Hypertension: Continued home Lisinopril 10mg daily.

# Obstructive sleep apnea: Continued home CPAP.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis  //
steroid injection R hip

TECHNIQUE:  The procedure was supervised by Dr. ___, the attending
radiologist, who was present for the critical portions of the procedure.

COMPARISON:  Fluoroscopic guided injection of the right hip ___

PROCEDURE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives were explained to the
patient and written informed consent obtained.

A pre-procedure timeout confirmed three patient identifiers.

Under fluoroscopic guidance, an appropriate spot was marked. The area was
prepared and draped in standard sterile fashion.

3 cc 1% Lidocaine was used to achieve local anesthesia. Under intermittent
fluoroscopic guidance, a 20-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the right 
hip joint. Appropriate position was confirmed by the injection of a small
amount of water soluble contrast.  A mixture of 3 cc of 0.25% Bupivacaine and
2 cc of Kenalog (Total 80 mg) was injected, dispersing the contrast.

The needle was removed, hemostasis achieved, and a sterile bandage applied. 
The patient experienced no significant change in symptoms immediately
following the procedure.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and left the department in stable
condition. There were no immediate complications or complaints.

FINDINGS: 

Contrast is seen within the right hip joint confirming intra-articular
extension

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful therapeutic injection into the right  hip joint.
